description: Walla Walla Vallis is a ancient valley in the equatorial region on Mars. It was carved during the wetter Noachian or Hesperian period by fluvial or groundwater-sapping processes, preserving a record of ancient water movement across the Martian landscape. Named for River in Washington, USA.

name: Warrego Valles
description: Warrego Valles is a valley system in the southern mid-latitudes on Mars. It was incised by ancient fluvial processes including possible outflow flooding or valley-network formation, preserving a record of ancient water movement across the Martian landscape. Named for Modern Australian River.

name: Wenjiashi Mensa
description: Wenjiashi Mensa is a flat-topped mesa or table mountain in the equatorial region on Mars, typically isolated by erosion from a formerly more extensive plateau. Named for Named for nearby crater, Wenjiashi.

name: Xanthe Patera
description: Xanthe Patera is a volcanic caldera or patera complex in the equatorial region adjacent to the Tharsis volcanic province. Its low-relief or collapsed form records the drainage of a shallow magma reservoir, and its degradation state reflects the age of volcanic activity in this region. Named for Named for classical albedo feature name, Xanthe.

name: Yaodian Fossae
description: Yaodian Fossae is a system of elongate fractures and graben in the equatorial region on Mars. It formed by extensional tectonics linked to volcanic loading or crustal stress, recording the broad reach of Martian tectonic deformation. Named for Named for nearby crater, Yaodian.

name: Zarqa Valles
description: Zarqa Valles is a ancient valley in the equatorial region on Mars. It was carved during the wetter Noachian or Hesperian period by fluvial or groundwater-sapping processes, preserving a record of ancient water movement across the Martian landscape. Named for River in Jordan.

name: Zephyria Mensae
description: Zephyria Mensae is a flat-topped mesa or table mountain in the equatorial region on Mars, typically isolated by erosion from a formerly more extensive plateau. Named for Albedo feature name.

name: Zephyrus Fossae
description: Zephyrus Fossae is a system of elongate fractures and graben in the equatorial region on Mars in the Elysium volcanic province. It formed by extensional tectonics linked to volcanic loading or crustal stress, recording the broad reach of Martian tectonic deformation. Named for Albedo feature name.

name: Zeus Patera
description: Zeus Patera is a volcanic caldera or patera complex in the equatorial region adjacent to the Tharsis volcanic province. Its low-relief or collapsed form records the drainage of a shallow magma reservoir, and its degradation state reflects the age of volcanic activity in this region. Named for Greek sky, thunder and lightning god, who ruled as king of the gods of Mount Olympus.

name: Cassini
description: Cassini is a large degraded impact crater 408 km across in the equatorial region on Mars. Its 408 km diameter places it among the large degraded craters of the Martian surface, with a heavily modified basin with an eroded rim and extensively infilled interior. Named for Giovanni; Italian astronomer (1625-1712).

name: Antoniadi
description: Antoniadi is a large degraded impact crater 401 km across in the equatorial region on Mars. Its 401 km diameter places it among the large degraded craters of the Martian surface, with a heavily modified basin with an eroded rim and extensively infilled interior. Named for Eugène Michael; Turkish-born French astronomer (1870-1944).

name: Acheron Fossae
description: A system of extensional fractures and graben northwest of Olympus Mons on the outer margin of the Tharsis bulge. Among the northernmost of the radial tectonic features generated by Tharsis loading, its fracture traces document the immense reach of volcanic and tectonic stresses from the Tharsis rise.

name: Acidalia Planitia
description: A broad 2,600-km lowland plain in the northern hemisphere important for studying sediment redistribution, possible mud volcanism, and polar ice-related processes. Its dark surface markings were historically mapped as one of Mars's most prominent albedo features.

name: Aeolis Mons
description: Also called Mount Sharp, the central layered mound within Gale Crater rising above the crater floor. Its stacked sequences of sedimentary layers record billions of years of changing climate, water chemistry, and depositional environments explored by Curiosity.

name: Aeolis Palus
description: Aeolis Palus is a historical albedo region or marsh-like feature in the equatorial region on Mars, identified from early telescopic observations. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Aeolis Serpens
description: Aeolis Serpens is a sinuous ridge or serpentine feature in the equatorial region on Mars, possibly an inverted channel or esker-like deposit recording ancient water or lava flow. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Alba Mons
description: An enormous low-relief volcanic rise north of Tharsis, notable for its extraordinary lateral extent relative to its height. Its broad topography records long-duration effusive volcanism spread across an exceptionally wide area, distinct from the steep edifices of the Tharsis Montes.

name: Albor Tholus
description: A smaller Elysium volcanic centre with a well-defined summit caldera, helping show that Elysium volcanism involved multiple constructional centres rather than one isolated edifice. Intermediate in size between Elysium Mons and smaller regional tholii.

name: Amazonis Planitia
description: A broad, smooth western lowland plain with one of the lowest crater densities on Mars, indicating volcanic resurfacing well into the Amazonian period. Radar data suggests ice-rich subsurface layers beneath its smooth surface.

name: Amazonis Sulci
description: Amazonis Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Albedo feature name; home of the Amazons.

name: Amenthes Cavi
description: Amenthes Cavi is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Amphitrites Patera
description: A large, heavily eroded Noachian volcanic caldera complex southeast of Hellas Basin with a diameter of. One of the oldest volcanic features on Mars, it may have interacted with hydrothermal systems generated by the Hellas impact.

name: Anseris Cavus
description: Anseris Cavus is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Named for albedo feature Anseris Fons. Same feature as Peraea Cavus.

name: Apollinaris Mons
description: An isolated volcano east of the main Tharsis province with a distinctive fan-shaped apron of pyroclastic debris on its southern flank. Its isolated position and distinct morphology make it valuable for comparing volcanic construction with the major Tharsis rises.

name: Apollinaris Sulci
description: Apollinaris Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Albedo feature at 5S, 187W.

name: Arabia Terra
description: A heavily cratered ancient terrain in the northern mid-latitudes preserving some of the oldest Martian crust. It contains abundant clay minerals, valley networks, and possible paleolake deposits recording prolonged early Martian aqueous activity.

name: Arcadia Planitia
description: A northern mid-latitude plain with high concentrations of near-surface ground ice indicated by polygonal terrain, lobate debris aprons, and scalloped depressions. Considered a prime target for future human exploration due to its accessible latitude, flat terrain, and retrievable ice resources.

name: Ares Vallis
description: A major Hesperian outflow channel draining chaotic terrain into Chryse Planitia. Mars Pathfinder landed here in 1997 among flood-deposited boulders from diverse source regions, effectively sampling Mars's geological diversity.

name: Argyre Cavi
description: Argyre Cavi is a depression or hollow in the southern high latitudes on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Albedo name.

name: Argyre Planitia
description: A giant ~1,800-km southern hemisphere impact basin with a floor 5 km below the surrounding highlands. Its topography strongly shaped regional drainage and sediment movement, and its rim channels preserve evidence for early Martian water flow.

name: Arsia Mons
description: The southernmost Tharsis volcano and the one with the largest summit caldera (). Its extensive volcanic apron, pit-chain systems, and evidence for late Amazonian glaciation make it one of the most geologically complex Tharsis edifices.

name: Arsia Sulci
description: Arsia Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Albedo name.

name: Ascraeus Mons
description: The northernmost of the three aligned Tharsis Montes shield volcanoes, rising above datum with a summit caldera complex. Its radially distributed lava flows and nested calderas record multiple major eruptive episodes spanning billions of years.

name: Ascraeus Sulci
description: Ascraeus Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Classical albedo name.

name: Athabasca Valles
description: One of the youngest outflow channels on Mars, originating from Cerberus Fossae with an extremely low crater density indicating formation within the last few million years. Its pristine morphology records one of the most recent catastrophic volatile release events, likely involving both lava and liquid water.

name: Ausonia Cavus
description: Ausonia Cavus is a depression or hollow in the southern mid-latitudes on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Albedo feature Ausonia.

name: Australe Lingula
description: Australe Lingula is a tongue-shaped extension of the polar layered deposits in the south polar region. Such features mark the irregular margins of polar ice caps and preserve records of recent climate change. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Australe Sulci
description: Australe Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the south polar region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Avernus Cavi
description: Avernus Cavi is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Named for albedo feature at 10S, 195W.

name: Baetis Labēs
description: Baetis Labēs is a landslide deposit in the equatorial region on Mars, recording a large-scale mass-wasting event from a nearby canyon wall or escarpment. Named for Classical albedo feature, Baetis.

name: Biblis Patera
description: A small shield volcano and shallow caldera complex on the southern Tharsis rise, representing one of the smaller volcanic constructs of the province. May have been active into the Amazonian period based on low-crater-density lava surfaces.

name: Boreum Cavus
description: Boreum Cavus is a depression or hollow in the north polar region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Candor Chasma
description: A large interior Valles Marineris basin containing thick Interior Layered Deposits of finely laminated light-toned sediments with hydrated sulfate minerals. The deposits are interpreted as lacustrine, aeolian, or volcanic ash accumulations in a long-lived closed basin.

name: Candor Labes
description: Candor Labes is a landslide deposit in the equatorial region on Mars, recording a large-scale mass-wasting event from a nearby canyon wall or escarpment. Named for From classical albedo feature at 5N, 75W.

name: Candor Sulci
description: Candor Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Cantabras Serpens
description: Cantabras Serpens is a sinuous ridge or serpentine feature in the equatorial region on Mars, possibly an inverted channel or esker-like deposit recording ancient water or lava flow. Named for From nearby albedo feature Cantabras, at 10N, 5W.

name: Cavi Angusti
description: Cavi Angusti is a depression or hollow in the south polar region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Cavi Frigorēs
description: Cavi Frigorēs is a depression or hollow in the south polar region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for From classical albedo feature Polus Frigoris, at 84S, 30W. Name dropped Sept. 2006, and area covered by this feature included with Cavi Angusti.

name: Cavi Novi
description: Cavi Novi is a depression or hollow in the south polar region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name; (dropped 1984).

name: Ceraunius Fossae
description: A system of radial graben and fractures extending north from Ceraunius Tholus across the northern Tharsis plateau. Formed by tensional stresses from Tharsis volcanic loading and magmatic intrusion, they are among the best-preserved fossae of the province.

name: Ceraunius Tholus
description: A moderately sized Tharsis shield volcano with a well-defined summit caldera flanked by sinuous rilles and valley networks, possibly carved by volcanic or hydrothermal processes melting surface ice. Active during the Hesperian period.

name: Cerberus Fossae
description: Young tectonic fissures cutting across Elysium Planitia, linked to the most recent geologically active region on Mars. The fissures sourced young lava flows and possibly late groundwater release, and InSight detected marsquakes emanating from this system.

name: Cerberus Palus
description: Cerberus Palus is a historical albedo region or marsh-like feature in the equatorial region on Mars, identified from early telescopic observations. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Ceti Labes
description: Ceti Labes is a landslide deposit in the equatorial region on Mars, recording a large-scale mass-wasting event from a nearby canyon wall or escarpment. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Chasma Boreale
description: A 560-km re-entrant trough cutting into the north polar layered deposits, exposing hundreds of alternating ice and dust layers in its walls. These layers record millions of years of climate cycles driven by Martian orbital variations (obliquity and eccentricity).

name: Chryse Planitia
description: A lowland sink for several major outflow channel systems draining from the Tharsis region, preserving evidence for catastrophic flooding. Viking 1 (1976) and Pathfinder (1997) both landed here, finding flood-transported boulders and diverse rock assemblages.

name: Claritas Fossae
description: A prominent north-south trending system of fractures and graben on the southwestern Tharsis plateau forming the western boundary of the Thaumasia highland block. Among the oldest tectonic structures in the Tharsis region, pre-dating many of the large volcanic shields.

name: Coprates Chasma
description: The long central-south trough of Valles Marineris, and over 8 km deep. It connects the eastern chaotic terrain with the Melas-Candor basin to the west, exposing an ancient crustal cross-section through billions of years of Martian geology.

name: Coprates Labes
description: Coprates Labes is a landslide deposit in the equatorial region on Mars, recording a large-scale mass-wasting event from a nearby canyon wall or escarpment. Named for From albedo feature at 14S, 65W.

name: Cyane Sulci
description: Cyane Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Daedalia Planum
description: A vast young lava plain extending southwest of Tharsis, largely fed by flows from Arsia Mons. Its exceptionally low crater density confirms eruptions well into the Amazonian period, making it among the youngest large volcanic surfaces on Mars.

name: Dalu Cavus
description: Dalu Cavus is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Javanese word for night.

name: Dao Vallis
description: A ~1,100-km outflow channel on the southeastern Hellas rim, likely formed by volcanic heating mobilising subsurface ice or groundwater. Its origin near the giant impact basin links volcanism, the Hellas thermal anomaly, and catastrophic water release.

name: Deuteronilus Cavus
description: Deuteronilus Cavus is a depression or hollow in the northern mid-latitudes on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Named from albedo feature at 35N, 355W.

name: Echus Chasma
description: A large canyon north of Valles Marineris that served as the primary source region for the Kasei Valles outflow system. Its enormous 100-km-wide headwall alcove records catastrophic water release events that carved one of Mars's largest outflow channel networks downstream.

name: Echus Palus
description: Echus Palus is a historical albedo region or marsh-like feature in the equatorial region on Mars, identified from early telescopic observations. Named for Classical albedo feature name, Echus Lacus.

name: Elysium Mons
description: The largest volcano in the Elysium volcanic province at elevation, built by sustained basaltic shield-building eruptions. It represents significant large-scale volcanism outside the Tharsis rise and has a caldera.

name: Elysium Planitia
description: A young volcanic plain hosting the InSight lander and crossed by Cerberus Fossae fissures. Radar and surface data reveal very recent lava emplacement and possible subsurface ice interactions, making it one of the most geologically active regions on present-day Mars.

name: Galaxias Fluctūs
description: Galaxias Fluctūs is a lava flow field in the northern mid-latitudes on Mars in the Elysium volcanic province, extending. It records a large-scale effusive eruption that resurfaced a significant area with basaltic lava. Named for Albedo feature name.

name: Ganges Cavus
description: Ganges Cavus is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Gemina Lingula
description: Gemina Lingula is a tongue-shaped extension of the polar layered deposits in the north polar region. Such features mark the irregular margins of polar ice caps and preserve records of recent climate change. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Gigas Sulci
description: Gigas Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Granicus Valles
description: An outflow channel system in the Elysium volcanic province, likely carved by catastrophic floods sourced from the Elysium rise. Its channel morphology and relationship to surrounding lava plains help constrain the timing of Elysium volcanism and associated volatile release.

name: Hadriaca Patera
description: An old volcanic complex northeast of Hellas with a broad, low-relief caldera and extensive channel networks on its flanks, possibly carved by explosive eruptions and hydrothermal processes. Its eroded form preserves evidence for volatile-rich volcanic activity in early Mars.

name: Hadriacus Cavi
description: Hadriacus Cavi is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Hadriacus Palus
description: Hadriacus Palus is a historical albedo region or marsh-like feature in the equatorial region on Mars, identified from early telescopic observations. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Hecates Tholus
description: A volcanic edifice in the Elysium province with a summit caldera and flanks modified by lava flows, collapse features, and possible water-ice interaction. Its relatively steep profile and volatile-rich history make it a target for studying Elysium's eruptive history.

name: Hellas Planitia
description: One of the largest confirmed impact structures in the Solar System, and 7–8 km deep. Its extreme depth creates unique atmospheric pressure conditions and strongly influences regional weather, ice stability, and sediment transport.

name: Hesperia Planum
description: The type locality of the Hesperian period, a broad southern mid-latitude lava plain defined by compressional wrinkle ridges formed by thermal contraction of flood basalts. Central to establishing the Martian geologic timescale.

name: Hiddekel Cavus
description: Hiddekel Cavus is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name, Hiddekel.

name: Hrad Vallis
description: An outflow channel on the northwestern flank of Elysium Mons, formed when volcanic eruptions melted ground ice or mobilised groundwater along grabens from the Elysium rise. Its morphology and deposits suggest a combination of lava emplacement and catastrophic water release.

name: Hydrae Cavus
description: Hydrae Cavus is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Hyperborea Lingula
description: Hyperborea Lingula is a tongue-shaped extension of the polar layered deposits in the north polar region. Such features mark the irregular margins of polar ice caps and preserve records of recent climate change. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Hyperborei Cavi
description: Hyperborei Cavi is a depression or hollow in the north polar region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Isidis Planitia
description: A large ancient impact basin on the highland-lowland boundary. Its rim and floor record the interaction of impact processes, volcanism (Syrtis Major lavas), and later sedimentary resurfacing, and it hosted the Beagle 2 and InSight missions.

name: Ismenius Cavus
description: Ismenius Cavus is a depression or hollow in the northern mid-latitudes on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Ismenius Lacus
description: A transitional region between the ancient southern highlands and northern lowlands, marked by well-developed fretted terrain of isolated mesas and flat-floored valleys created by mass wasting, sublimation, and ice-driven erosion along the dichotomy boundary.

name: Ius Chasma
description: The westernmost major trough of Valles Marineris,, with walls exposing layered sulfates and phyllosilicates deposited under different aqueous conditions. Its floor preserves large landslide deposits and possible evaporite sequences from ancient water ponding.

name: Ius Labes
description: Ius Labes is a landslide deposit in the equatorial region on Mars, recording a large-scale mass-wasting event from a nearby canyon wall or escarpment. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Jovis Tholus
description: A small dome-shaped volcanic construct in central Tharsis with a summit caldera and relatively steep flanks, suggesting a more viscous eruptive history than the large adjacent shields. Its compact form may reflect limited magma supply or a shorter-lived volcanic centre.

name: Juventae Cavi
description: Juventae Cavi is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Kasei Valles
description: One of Mars's largest outflow channel systems, stretching from Echus Chasma into Chryse Planitia. Multiple flood events carved the branching channel complex, moving estimated water volumes equivalent to large terrestrial seas.

name: Krishnan Palus
description: Krishnan Palus is a historical albedo region or marsh-like feature in the equatorial region on Mars, identified from early telescopic observations. Named for Named from nearby crater, Krishnan.

name: Labeatis Fossae
description: Radially oriented fractures and graben on the Tharsis Plateau driven by extensional tectonics from the volcanic rise's mass and magmatic inflation, documenting the scale and long duration of Tharsis-related tectonic activity.

name: Layl Cavus
description: Layl Cavus is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Arabic word for night.

name: Lunae Planum
description: A high Hesperian lava plateau between Valles Marineris and Chryse Planitia, bounded by steep escarpments and deeply incised by Kasei Valles. Its smooth surface records extensive Tharsis-fed lava emplacement during the Hesperian.

name: Lycus Sulci
description: Lycus Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Ma'adim Vallis
description: One of the largest ancient valley systems on Mars, stretching northward into Gusev Crater. Thought to have been carved by catastrophic drainage of a Noachian highland lake, it is a primary feature for reconstructing early Martian hydrology and lacustrine systems.

name: Maja Valles
description: A large outflow channel draining from Lunae Planum plateau into Chryse Planitia via a broad anastomosing network. Its channel complex records multiple catastrophic flood events that transported enormous volumes of water and sediment northward during the Hesperian.

name: Malam Cavus
description: Malam Cavus is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Indonesian word for night.

name: Malea Patera
description: A heavily degraded ancient volcanic caldera southwest of Hellas Basin, part of the circum-Hellas volcanic province. Like its neighbours Amphitrites and Peneus Paterae, it records Noachian-era volcanism possibly amplified by deep fractures associated with the Hellas impact.

name: Malea Planum
description: A Hesperian-aged ridged volcanic plain south of Hellas Basin characterised by compressional wrinkle ridges formed by the cooling and contraction of extensive flood basalt eruptions. Its ridge pattern records a globally significant episode of Martian flood volcanism during the Hesperian.

name: Mangala Valles
description: A major ~900-km outflow system likely sourced by sudden pressurised groundwater release along tectonic fractures in the Tharsis margin. It records the coupling between Tharsis volcanism, crustal stress, and catastrophic flooding.

name: Mawrth Vallis
description: A heavily studied ancient valley system surrounded by clay-rich rocks including Fe/Mg smectites and Al-phyllosilicates indicating prolonged Noachian aqueous alteration. One of the most mineralogically diverse ancient terrains on Mars and a strong astrobiology target.

name: Medusae Sulci
description: Medusae Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Albedo feature name.

name: Melas Chasma
description: One of the deepest sections of Valles Marineris, below the surrounding plateau rim. It contains thick Interior Layered Deposits including sulfate minerals interpreted as evaporites, and its floor records episodic ponding and sediment infill.

name: Melas Labes
description: Melas Labes is a landslide deposit in the equatorial region on Mars, recording a large-scale mass-wasting event from a nearby canyon wall or escarpment. Named for From albedo feature at 10S, 74W.

name: Memnonia Sulci
description: Memnonia Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Albedo feature name.

name: Meridiani Planum
description: A sedimentary plain rich in crystalline grey hematite and sulfate-bearing layered rock explored by the Opportunity rover (2004–2018). Central to studies of ancient acidic aqueous environments, it hosts outcrops recording episodic wetting in a largely desiccated environment.

name: Meridiani Serpentes
description: Meridiani Serpentes is a sinuous ridge or serpentine feature in the equatorial region on Mars, possibly an inverted channel or esker-like deposit recording ancient water or lava flow. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Meroe Patera
description: One of two summit calderas on Syrtis Major Planum, named after the ancient city of Meroe. A shallow collapse depression overlying a solidified magma system inferred from gravity data to be at least 5 km thick beneath the surface.

name: Nat Cavus
description: Nat Cavus is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Danish word for night.

name: Nili Fossae
description: A system of concentric fractures and troughs the Isidis basin rim, exposing mineral-rich crust including clays, carbonates, and olivine. One of the largest carbonate exposures on Mars and a major astrobiology target for recording early habitable environments.

name: Nili Patera
description: The more studied of Syrtis Major's two summit calderas, attracting strong interest for its geologically recent activity. It hosts fresh hydrothermal mineral signatures and actively migrating dunes, placing it among the most geologically dynamic surface sites on present-day Mars.

name: Nirgal Vallis
description: A ~500-km branching valley network in the southern highlands with theatre-headed tributaries consistent with groundwater sapping processes. One of the most studied examples of ancient valley formation on Mars and key to debates about groundwater vs. precipitation-fed incision.

name: Noachis Terra
description: The type locality defining Mars's Noachian period, a densely cratered ancient southern terrain extensively dissected by valley networks formed under an early wetter climate. It preserves the geological record of the earliest billion years of Martian surface history.

name: Noc Cavus
description: Noc Cavus is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Polish word for night.

name: Noctis Fossae
description: A dense network of fractures and graben west of Noctis Labyrinthus on the Tharsis plateau, formed by the same extensional stresses that created the broader Valles Marineris rift system to the east. They help trace the propagation of Tharsis-driven extension westward.

name: Noctis Labyrinthus
description: A maze of intersecting grabens and collapsed blocks at the western end of Valles Marineris. It records intense crustal extension and collapse tied to Tharsis uplift, with hydrated minerals and possible recent volcanic activity in its floor.

name: Octantis Cavi
description: Octantis Cavi is a depression or hollow in the southern high latitudes on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Albedo name.

name: Oenotria Cavi
description: Oenotria Cavi is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name, Oenotria.

name: Olympia Cavi
description: Olympia Cavi is a depression or hollow in the north polar region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Olympica Fossae
description: A fracture system of radial graben extending from the Olympus Mons escarpment, tracing the tectonic stress field of the Tharsis volcanic rise. Among the longest radial fracture systems associated with Olympus Mons loading.

name: Olympus Maculae
description: Olympus Maculae is a dark spot or irregular dark marking in the equatorial region on Mars. Such features typically correspond to dust-free or mineralogically distinct exposures. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Olympus Mons
description: The tallest known volcano in the Solar System at above datum. Olympus Mons is a giant shield volcano built by long-lived low-viscosity basaltic eruptions on Mars's mostly static crust, with a basal scarp up to 8 km high and a summit caldera complex 80 km across.

name: Ophir Cavus
description: Ophir Cavus is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Ophir Chasma
description: A northern Valles Marineris trough with kilometre-scale walls exposing ancient crustal stratigraphy including layered sulfates and iron oxides. Large interior landslide deposits record episodic wall collapse during the canyon's development.

name: Ophir Labes
description: Ophir Labes is a landslide deposit in the equatorial region on Mars, recording a large-scale mass-wasting event from a nearby canyon wall or escarpment. Named for From albedo feature at 10S, 65W.

name: Oxus Cavus
description: Oxus Cavus is a depression or hollow in the northern mid-latitudes on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Pavonis Mons
description: The central volcano of the Tharsis Montes chain, notable for straddling Mars's equator. Its summit caldera sits atop a broad shield and is flanked by pit chains and radial graben recording the complex interplay of volcanism and tectonic extension.

name: Pavonis Sulci
description: Pavonis Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Albedo name.

name: Peneus Palus
description: Peneus Palus is a historical albedo region or marsh-like feature in the southern mid-latitudes on Mars, identified from early telescopic observations. Named for From classical albedo feature at 48S, 290W.

name: Peneus Patera
description: An ancient degraded patera on the southern Hellas rim, part of a cluster of old calderas modified by billions of years of erosion and ice. Its proximity to Hellas invites comparisons with basin-driven hydrothermal activity in early Mars.

name: Peraea Cavus
description: Peraea Cavus is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Albedo feature name.

name: Piscinas Serpentes
description: Piscinas Serpentes is a sinuous ridge or serpentine feature in the equatorial region on Mars, possibly an inverted channel or esker-like deposit recording ancient water or lava flow. Named for Named for nearby Piscinas crater.

name: Pityusa Patera
description: The largest of the highland paterae around Hellas Basin, with a caldera complex so vast it is comparable in area to Olympus Mons. Its immense size makes it one of the most extraordinary ancient volcanic structures on Mars despite its heavily eroded Noachian state.

name: Planum Australe
description: The southern polar layered deposits capped by a permanent CO₂ ice sheet ~8 m thick covering a water ice base up to 3.7 km thick. MARSIS radar data suggests possible liquid water at the base, making it a focus for subsurface habitability research.

name: Planum Boreum
description: The northern polar layered deposits, a 1,000-km-wide stack of alternating water-ice and dust layers up to 3 km thick. Radar profiling reveals 100+ individual layers that archive climate variations driven by Martian orbital cycles over millions of years.

name: Promethei Lingula
description: Promethei Lingula is a tongue-shaped extension of the polar layered deposits in the south polar region. Such features mark the irregular margins of polar ice caps and preserve records of recent climate change. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Promethei Terra
description: Heavily cratered ancient terrain between Hellas Basin and the south polar cap, showing extensive glacial modification including lobate debris aprons and lineated valley fills. Key for understanding the interaction of ancient impact tectonics with polar ice dynamics.

name: Reull Vallis
description: An ancient ~1,600-km valley in the southern highlands with terraced walls and braided floor morphology indicating both fluvial incision and subsequent glacial modification across different Martian climate epochs spanning the Noachian to Amazonian.

name: Sacra Fossae
description: Fractures and graben on the margin of Lunae Planum radiating outward from the Tharsis bulge. They document the far-reaching tectonic influence of the volcanic rise on the surrounding lithosphere and mark the boundary of the plateau.

name: Sacra Sulci
description: Sacra Sulci is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for From albedo feature at 20N, 67W.

name: Scandia Cavi
description: Scandia Cavi is a depression or hollow in the north polar region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Named for classical albedo feature at 65N, 150W.

name: Simud Valles
description: A major Hesperian outflow channel draining northward from chaotic terrain into Chryse Planitia. Part of the massive flood system that shaped the Chryse lowland, transporting vast sediment and boulder loads from the Margaritifer Chaos region.

name: Sinai Planum
description: One of the elevated volcanic plateaus of the central Tharsis rise between Syria and Solis Plana. Its smooth lava-covered surface and high elevation mark it as part of the summit region of the Tharsis bulge where the highest Martian plateau elevations occur.

name: Sisyphi Cavi
description: Sisyphi Cavi is a depression or hollow in the south polar region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Sisyphi Tholus
description: One of the southernmost identified volcanic constructs on Mars near the south polar region, with a summit caldera indicating past magmatic activity at high southern latitudes. Evidence that Martian volcanism spanned a wide latitudinal range.

name: Solis Planum
description: A broad plateau south of Tharsis shaped by Tharsis-related volcanism and extensional tectonics. It grades into the fractured Thaumasia Planum to the south and the Valles Marineris canyon systems to the north, recording the transition from volcanic plateau to rift terrain.

name: Sulci Gordii
description: Sulci Gordii is a set of parallel furrows and ridges in the equatorial region on Mars. Sulci on Mars typically record intense tectonic deformation or possibly tidal stressing in ancient terrain. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Syria Planum
description: The broad volcanic plateau at the topographic centre of the Tharsis rise, sitting atop the convergence of the three Tharsis Montes. Its elevated position and thick lava stack form the topographic core from which the Tharsis volcanic province radiates outward.

name: Syrtis Major Planum
description: A dark low-relief volcanic plateau, one of the most prominent telescopic features of Mars. Its olivine-basalt surface records Hesperian flood volcanism and is bordered by rich clay and carbonate mineral deposits in Nili Fossae.

name: Tantalus Fluctus
description: Tantalus Fluctus is a lava flow field in the northern mid-latitudes on Mars on the Tharsis rise, extending. It records a large-scale effusive eruption that resurfaced a significant area with basaltic lava. Named for Albedo feature name.

name: Tantalus Fossae
description: A system of extensional fractures and graben on the northeastern flank of Alba Mons, formed by tensional stresses from Tharsis volcanic loading. Among the northernmost tectonic features directly tied to the Tharsis province's crustal stress field.

name: Tempe Terra
description: A faulted highland plateau on the edge of Tharsis recording regional crustal extension and deformation. Its complex network of graben and normal faults documents the broad tectonic influence of the Tharsis rise on the surrounding lithosphere.

name: Tenuis Cavus
description: Tenuis Cavus is a depression or hollow in the north polar region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Terra Cimmeria
description: A broad southern highland province preserving ancient densely cratered crust with a strong remnant crustal magnetic signature. Its long-term weathering and resurfacing record makes it important for understanding early Mars crustal evolution.

name: Terra Sabaea
description: An ancient southern highland bordering Syrtis Major and the northwestern Hellas rim, with densely cratered crust and widespread phyllosilicate minerals in valley walls. Records prolonged Noachian water-rock interaction and early chemical weathering under aqueous conditions.

name: Terra Sirenum
description: An old southern highland preserving among the strongest remnant crustal magnetic anomalies on Mars. Its heavily cratered surface records some of the earliest preserved surface history and shows evidence for chloride-bearing deposits formed in ancient evaporating water bodies.

name: Tharsis Tholus
description: An isolated intermediate shield volcano on the eastern Tharsis rise with a well-preserved caldera containing multiple collapse pits. Built by repeated low-viscosity lava eruptions and represents an intermediate-scale construct between the massive shields and smaller tholii.

name: Thaumasia Planum
description: A faulted plateau south of Valles Marineris shaped by Tharsis-driven extension and compressional folding. Its complex structural geology records the broad crustal deformation field generated by the Tharsis volcanic load and the southward propagation of the Valles Marineris rift.

name: Thymiamata Serpens
description: Thymiamata Serpens is a sinuous ridge or serpentine feature in the equatorial region on Mars, possibly an inverted channel or esker-like deposit recording ancient water or lava flow. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Tinjar Valles
description: A northern Elysium outflow channel system draining away from the Elysium rise, recording the close coupling between Elysium volcanism and catastrophic volatile release. Like Granicus and Athabasca Valles, it formed during the Amazonian period.

name: Tiu Valles
description: A complex outflow channel system adjacent to Simud Valles, originating in chaotic collapsed terrain and debouching into Chryse Planitia. Together with Ares and Simud Valles it forms part of the great Hesperian flood network that shaped the northern plains.

name: Tyrrhena Patera
description: A heavily degraded ancient Noachian/Hesperian volcanic centre with a large shallow caldera complex surrounded by radial channels. Among the oldest identifiable volcanic structures on Mars, it records an early explosive phase of Martian volcanism dominated by volatile-rich magmas.

name: Tyrrhena Terra
description: An ancient volcanic highland terrain associated with Tyrrhena Patera, preserving some of the oldest large-scale Martian volcanism from the Noachian and early Hesperian. A key province for understanding Mars volcanism before Tharsis dominated.

name: Ultima Lingula
description: Ultima Lingula is a tongue-shaped extension of the polar layered deposits in the south polar region. Such features mark the irregular margins of polar ice caps and preserve records of recent climate change. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Ultimi Cavi
description: Ultimi Cavi is a depression or hollow in the south polar region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for See Thyles Rupes; name dropped 1984.

name: Ulysses Patera
description: A collapsed summit caldera on the Tharsis Plateau closely associated with Biblis Patera. Multiple collapse cycles indicate repeated magma withdrawal beneath the low shield structure, and its relatively pristine morphology suggests activity into the Amazonian.

name: Uranius Mons
description: A large shield volcano in the northern Tharsis region with a broad gently sloping edifice and summit caldera complex. Its flanking rift structures and associated pit chains suggest multiple episodes of volcanic activity spanning the Hesperian and Amazonian periods.

name: Usiku Cavus
description: Usiku Cavus is a depression or hollow in the equatorial region on Mars, formed by subsurface collapse, sublimation of volatiles, or dissolution of subsurface materials. Named for Swahili word for night.

name: Utopia Planitia
description: A broad ~3,300-km lowland basin in Mars's northern plains and the largest recognised impact basin on Mars. Radar sounding reveals enormous subsurface ice deposits, and Viking 2 landed here in 1976.

name: Valles Marineris
description: A vast canyon network stretching equatorial Mars, up to 7 km deep and 200 km wide. It exposes billions of years of layered crustal stratigraphy including sulfates and phyllosilicates, recording tectonic extension, collapse, and ancient aqueous activity.

name: Vastitas Borealis
description: The vast lowland plain dominating Mars's northern polar region, possibly the floor of an ancient ocean ('Oceanus Borealis'). Polygonal patterned ground and other periglacial features record ice-rich subsurface material across this immense terrain.

name: Zephyria Fluctus
description: Zephyria Fluctus is a lava flow field in the equatorial region on Mars in the Elysium volcanic province, extending. It records a large-scale effusive eruption that resurfaced a significant area with basaltic lava. Named for Classical albedo feature name.

name: Viking 1
description: NASA's Viking 1 lander touched down in Chryse Planitia on 20 July 1976, becoming the first spacecraft to operate successfully on the Martian surface. It conducted biology experiments, analysed soil chemistry, and returned the first colour images from Mars.

name: Viking 2
description: NASA's Viking 2 lander reached Utopia Planitia on 3 September 1976, extending the first generation of Mars surface science. It detected water-ice clouds and seasonal frost, and its biology experiments remain central to ongoing debates about Mars habitability.

name: Pathfinder
description: Mars Pathfinder landed in Ares Vallis flood deposits on 4 July 1997 and deployed Sojourner — the first rover to operate on another planet. Rock and soil analyses suggested the landing site had been reworked by catastrophic floods from diverse geological terrains.

name: Spirit
description: NASA's Spirit rover landed in Gusev Crater on 3 January 2004. Operating for over six years, it discovered compelling evidence for ancient hydrothermal activity in altered silica-rich rocks of the Columbia Hills.

name: Opportunity
description: NASA's Opportunity rover landed in Meridiani Planum on 25 January 2004 and operated for nearly 15 years. It documented ancient sulfate-bearing sedimentary rocks, hematite concretions, and multiple ancient wet episodes across Meridiani.

name: Phoenix
description: NASA's Phoenix lander reached the northern plains on 25 May 2008 and directly sampled water ice in the shallow subsurface — the first time water ice was directly confirmed on another planet. It also detected perchlorate salts in Martian soil.

name: Curiosity
description: NASA's Curiosity rover landed in Gale Crater on 6 August 2012 and remains active, climbing through layered sedimentary rock in Aeolis Mons. It confirmed past habitability, detected organics, and documented billions of years of changing Martian climate.

name: Beagle 2
description: ESA's Beagle 2 lander reached the surface in Isidis Planitia on 25 December 2003 but failed to fully deploy its solar panels. Orbital imagery in 2015 confirmed it landed intact but with one or more panels that did not open correctly.

name: InSight
description: NASA's InSight lander touched down in western Elysium Planitia on 26 November 2018. It recorded over 1,300 marsquakes and revealed Mars has a thin crust, a large liquid outer core, and a complex mantle structure.

name: Perseverance
description: NASA's Perseverance rover landed in Jezero Crater on 18 February 2021, caching rock and regolith samples for future return to Earth while investigating the ancient delta-lake environment for signs of past microbial life. It also deployed the Ingenuity helicopter.

name: Arcadia Habitat Candidate
description: Candidate future settlement zone in Arcadia Planitia, supported by broad flat terrain and widespread near-surface water ice accessible for ISRU at a favourable sub-60°N latitude. SHARAD radar confirms extensive ice deposits.

name: Utopia Ice Habitat Candidate
description: Candidate future settlement zone in Utopia Planitia, supported by mid-latitude water-ice radar detections, broad flat terrain, and favourable lowland elevation. Estimated subsurface ice volume exceeds that of Lake Superior.

name: Protonilus Mensae Habitat Candidate
description: Candidate future settlement zone at Protonilus Mensae along the dichotomy boundary, supported by debris-covered glaciers, lobate debris aprons, and accessible ice resources inferred from glacial landforms.

name: Deuteronilus Mensae Habitat Candidate
description: Candidate future settlement zone at Deuteronilus Mensae, supported by SHARAD radar detection of clean ice, polygonal ground, and glacial landforms at a mid-latitude accessible for human operations.

Its 363 km diameter places it among the large degraded craters of the Martian surface, with a heavily modified basin with an eroded rim and extensively infilled interior.
